Title: UMK supports student who lost parents in Gerik crash
Article:
KOTA BARU: Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) is providing welfare and psychological support to graduating student Husna Syakira Abd Halim, who lost her parents in a road crash.
The
crash occurred
on the East-West Highway in Gerik, Perak, early yesterday afternoon.
In a statement, UMK expressed its condolences and deep sorrow over the tragedy involving the Faculty of Entrepreneurship and Business student.
Husna Syakira is graduating with a Bachelor of Entrepreneurship (Logistics and Distribution Trade) with Honours. She was due to receive her degree at UMK's 16th Convocation Ceremony tomorrow.
Following the news, the university, through the Student Wellbeing Division of the Deputy Vice-Chancellor's Office (Student Affairs and Alumni), sent a team of officials, Student Representative Council representatives and a psychological officer to Gerik Hospital.
UMK said it would continue to support the family, including with welfare assistance and other arrangements, to ensure everything ran smoothly.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, in a Facebook post today, extended his condolences to Husna Syakira and her family over the loss of her parents.
He said the Ministry of Higher Education and UMK would support the family, including by handling the funeral arrangements.
Zambry also expressed sadness over the tragedy. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: When petrol pit stops prove perilous
Article:
WAS it some weakness in the supply chain or unscrupulous businesses trying to cash in on our heavily subsidised RON95 petrol? News of contaminated petrol  in some northern  states in the peninsula and  the damage it caused to motor engines  has been  widely reported.
The Petrol Dealers Association of Malaysia   pointed out that it was counter-intuitive for petrol station owners to adulterate their petrol.
"Such actions offer no economic benefit to operators. Instead, they could undermine customer confidence and hurt their businesses," it said. The association has welcomed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry's investigation into the wider fuel supply chain.
Investigating authorities must establish whether the  incidents are isolated cases of  poor maintenance of underground storage tanks or  weaknesses further up the supply chain.
Their investigations must  not drag on  indefinitely.
Laboratory testing is undoubtedly important but there should be a clear timeline for results, regular public updates and prompt disclosure of findings. If contamination is indeed proven, those responsible must face firm action.
This should include examining the accountability of petrol station operators, fuel suppliers and other parties involved in the storage, transportation and distribution of the fuel.
Enforcement action cannot just stop at the retail level if the problem lies elsewhere. Equally important is  consumer protection.
Motorists whose engines were damaged by  contaminated petrol deserve  a clear, hassle-free avenue for compensation.
Petrol companies and station operators also have a clear interest in seeing the matter resolved as speedily as possible.
The authorities should also consider more frequent and random inspections, stricter maintenance requirements for underground storage tanks and a more robust monitoring of fuel quality at different levels of the distribution process.
There have even been reports of the problem spreading  south to Selangor, where authorities inspected   a petrol station in Sungai Buloh and collected fuel samples for analysis on Oct 19. The results of the analysis, or whether any wrongdoing was  uncovered, remain unknown.
There must be greater urgency in getting to the root of this matter. If not, consumer confidence will erode further. RON95 is the choice for most Malaysian motorists and  the government subsidises it at a great cost  to ease the rising cost of living  burdening   households.
Unresolved cases of diluted petrol and mounting complaints emerging in other states only aggravate consumer woes.
There must be no complacency in getting to the bottom of the matter as soon as possible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Could hackers get inside my fridge?
Article:
FRIDGES and freezers at supermarkets in several countries in Europe were hit by a cyberattack on Monday that raised their temperatures.
It follows a similar attack in France last month that heated refrigeration units to up to 50 degrees Celsius, causing fires and spoiling food.
A similar spate of mysterious freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the United States in August is also being treated as a suspected hack, Reuters reported in October.
From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarm networks, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.
CAN HACKERS REALLY GET INTO MY FRIDGE?
In theory, yes. If a device is connected to the internet, directly or through an app, cloud service or home network, it can potentially be hacked.
In 2015, researchers demonstrated at a Las Vegas hacking conference how a Samsung smart refrigerator could be compromised, allowing them to intercept some of the internet traffic passing through the device.
In many cases, attackers are more interested in stealing data, disrupting services or using connected devices as a way into a larger network.
WHAT HOUSEHOLD DEVICES COULD BE HACKED?
The most common targets are devices connected to the internet and controlled remotely.
These include security cameras, video doorbells, alarm systems, smart locks, thermostats and central heating systems.
Smart appliances such as refrigerators, ovens and washing machines can also be vulnerable if they are connected to the wider internet. Even some toothbrushes are now internet-connected.
Routers, not appliances, account for more than three-quarters of all attacks on connected devices, according to security-industry data.
The number of such devices has grown rapidly as manufacturers have added internet connectivity to products that were once entirely mechanical.
WHAT COULD A HACKER ACTUALLY DO?
Once inside a device, a hacker can generally do one of two things: gather information or take control of the device.
A camera can show the inside of a home, a device with a microphone can pick up sound, and a compromised router can expose everything that travels through the network.
[[nid:1569399]]
Hackers who take control of a device can switch it on or off, change settings or lock users out of their accounts.
A compromised thermostat could affect heating, while a hacked freezer or refrigerator could disrupt temperature controls.
In more serious cases, attackers may use poorly secured devices to gain access to other systems on the same network or to steal personal information linked to online accounts.
COULD HACKERS TAKE OVER MY CAR, ELECTRICITY OR WATER SUPPLY?
Cybersecurity researchers have repeatedly demonstrated vulnerabilities in connected vehicles.
In 2015, researchers remotely took control of a moving Jeep through its internet-connected entertainment system, forcing the recall of about 1.4 million vehicles and the deployment of software fixes.
Nearly a decade later, researchers disclosed a flaw that allowed them to track, unlock and start certain Kia vehicles using only a licence plate number.
The researchers said they reported the vulnerabilities to Kia, which fixed them within months, and there was no evidence they had been exploited in real-world attacks.
Modern vehicles and aircraft are also designed with extensive safety and backup systems.
Critical infrastructure such as power and water networks generally has multiple layers of security, monitoring and regulation that are not present in consumer devices.
That does not mean they are immune from cyberattacks, but they are typically much harder targets than a household appliance connected to a home Wi-Fi network.
HOW CAN PEOPLE PROTECT THEIR DEVICES?
Cybersecurity experts generally recommend changing default passwords, enabling two-factor authentication where available and regularly installing software updates.
Consumers should also remove or replace devices that no longer receive security updates, keep most devices on a local network and only connect products to the wider internet when there is a clear reason to do so.
The simplest rule is often the most effective: the fewer connected devices you have, the fewer potential entry points exist for attackers.
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Overseas missions generate RM59.5bil in potential investments, says Miti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fourteen official visits and trade and investment missions led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani generated RM59.5 billion in potential investments between 2025 and September this year.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said the missions were carried out through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) and the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade).
Of the total potential investments, RM14.2 billion have been approved, and the remaining RM45.3 billion are at various stages of negotiation and are being continuously followed up, Miti added.
"On the breakdown of realised investments, a project typically takes between 18 and 24 months to materialise, depending on its scale and complexity and prevailing economic conditions," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply today.
It added that Mida would continue its follow-up efforts, monitoring and facilitation to ensure that identified investment opportunities are translated into actual project implementation.
On the trade front, Miti said official visits to countries including Kenya, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Türkiye, Japan, Italy, France, South Korea, China, Thailand, India and Russia had yielded positive results, generating RM6.77 billion in exports through high-level engagements.
"In addition, Matrade continues to diversify its export promotion efforts into new markets in Central Asia, Africa and Latin America.
"From January to September, these three regions collectively recorded a 23.06 per cent rise in exports to RM69.84 billion," Miti said.
It added that markets which recorded double-digit growth included Namibia (up 426.1 per cent), Angola (55.6 per cent), Brazil (41.0 per cent), Tanzania (35.9 per cent), Ethiopia (28.5 per cent) and Kenya (11.6 per cent).

Title: Fridge cyberattack hits supermarkets across Europe
Article:
STOCKHOLM: Grocery stores in at least seven European countries saw temperatures in their cold cases soar on Monday, with several confirming they had been hit by a cyberattack similar to one three weeks ago in France.
Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden were among those affected in the latest hacker attack.
Stores were forced to throw out food that had spoiled or risked being spoiled and restock their refrigeration units with fresh items.
Major French retailers said on Oct 12 that hundreds of store refrigeration systems were hit by a cyberattack, which also forced them to toss food and raised concerns about food security.
No one has claimed responsibility for either attack.
Carrefour Belgium on Monday reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores.
"It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," said spokesman Mich Vergauwen.
An Ikea Belgium spokeswoman likewise said a cyberattack hit its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, causing the temperature of freezers to rise suddenly in the early hours of Monday.
Chains Delhaize, Colruyt and Intermarche also experienced technical problems affecting their fridges in Belgium, while Delhaize reported that four of its stores in Luxembourg were also affected.
Belgian industrial refrigeration group Sabcobel said it had begun securing its installations after the October 12 attack in France, but around 10 percent were still not fixed and some were in the shops affected on Monday.
"If Sabcobel hadn't started this operation ... the impact would have been much more important," chief executive Stephan Moelans told AFP.
Musgrave, which owns Supervalu in Ireland, said 13 of its stores were affected, as were a small number of corner shops in the Netherlands.
In Sweden, chain Coop confirmed six of its around 800 stores had been hit by a cyberattack early Monday.
"We can confirm that it is a cyber incident. The problem has now been resolved and the fridges and freezers are working as normal," spokesman Carlos Cancino told AFP.
He said Coop did not know who was behind the attack, but noted that the affected stores had been connected to a 4G mobile network, not the updated 5G system, which made them "more exposed" to hackers.
Swedish chain Ica also said "a limited number" of its stores experienced refrigeration problems, but the group could not confirm a cyberattack was the cause.
[[nid:1569410]]
According to Ica spokesperson Helena Johansson, the affected stores were all connected to an external refrigeration control system provided by Danish manufacturer Danfoss – the same supplier targeted in the Oct 12 cyberattack on French retailers.
She referred all queries to Danfoss.
It has not responded to AFP's request for a comment.
One Ica store located in Sjobo, in southern Sweden, posted on Facebook that its fridges and freezers had "been hacked and they set the temperature at 50 degrees" Celsius.
In Finland, irregular temperatures had also been detected in a few smaller grocery stores belonging to the Kesko group.
"We are currently investigating the cause, and interference via the network has not yet been ruled out," Petri Kayhko, head of Kesko's corporate security, told AFP.
Roni Kokkola, an information security specialist at the National Cyber Security Centre at Finland's Transport and Communications Agency Traficom, would not rule out cyber interference "as far as Finland is concerned."
"We've seen this in Europe in the past few months, so it spreading beyond France to other countries has been expected," he told AFP.
"Nowadays it's very typical that all kinds of vulnerabilities are being exploited ever more actively and rapidly."
In Estonia, at least one supermarket was attacked by hackers who raised the temperature in the refrigeration units to 50C, public broadcaster ERR reported.
The units were older models delivered by Danfoss, similar to the ones targeted in the France attack, Jann Mutso, director of Kitman Coldtech, a manufacturer and distributor of advanced refrigeration systems, told ERR.
"The handwriting is the same, but I can't say more," Mutso said.
Following the attack in France, Danfoss told AFP that most of the affected equipment were "legacy" products which "no longer receive software or security updates."
EU food and agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen said at the time that "food security requires more attention at all levels."
The "exploitation of food" was now a "reality", he added.

Title: AI chatbots spewing US election falsehoods face scrutiny
Article:
DISPENSING misleading voter information, misidentifying candidates and regurgitating Russian propaganda, artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are sowing information chaos ahead of the United States midterm elections, say researchers.
Today's vote marks the first federal election in which millions of voters are actively relying on AI tools for political information, a trend that experts say is playing a key role in shaping the information ecosystem ahead of the polls.
But while chatbots can help debunk conspiracies and educate voters, multiple studies show they frequently draw on unreliable sources on the open web, eroding public trust and further polluting an Internet already plagued by election misinformation.
One recent study by Forum AI, a startup that evaluates AI models, found that almost 40 per cent of chatbots' answers to election-related queries contained at least one factual error.
When its researchers asked Anthropic's Claude why voters should elect Representative Don Davis from North Carolina, the chatbot listed "former school superintendent" among his credentials, confusing him with a different person.
The study, which examined eight models, also found that chatbots answered questions about voting logistics incorrectly more often than questions about candidates.
When Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash was asked about voting in Pennsylvania, the chatbot gave Nov 3 as the deadline to request a mail-in ballot. The actual deadline was a week earlier.
Chatbots also "put the wrong words in the mouths of candidates, officials and observers hundreds of times" and frequently cited "poor quality" sources, such as Reddit threads, said Forum AI.
"We're focused on helping voters find reliable information across our platforms," said Google in a statement, adding that it had "strict quality and policy protections" across its AI products on election topics.
Another concern among researchers was that chatbots were susceptible to foreign influence, sometimes repeating falsehoods that were widely debunked.
Late last month, AFP's fact-checkers debunked a likely AI-altered clip that purported to show a former student of Texas Senate candidate James Talarico accusing him of sexual misconduct.
The unfounded allegation bore the hallmarks of a Russian disinformation campaign.
Google's AI Overview regurgitated the allegation when it was prompted by the disinformation watchdog NewsGuard.
Two other leading AI tools it prompted, Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot, also repeated the false claim.
"AI chatbot users are at risk of being fooled by foreign influence operations and other bad actors," said NewsGuard in a separate study of 10 AI tools.
A subsequent test by AFP, conducted after the claim had been widely debunked, found the AI tools cited professional fact-checkers, reflecting how chatbot responses can be inconsistent.
Referring to NewsGuard's study, Google said "this issue was addressed as our systems quickly updated to surface the latest reporting on this topic".
Responding to the study, Microsoft said "this was a rapidly developing situation with limited reliable information available at the time of the initial query".
It said as more information became available, "Copilot reflected the updated context and identified the claim as fabricated".
Today's vote also marks what the London-based Institute for Strategic Dialogue called the first US election with AI tools built into every major tech platform.
In a recent survey by the nonpartisan National Conference on Citizenship, two in five Americans said they had used AI tools to search for election information, including candidates or ballot measures.
Only 40 per cent trust the tools with logistical information, such as when, where and how to vote, and 60 per cent said they "trust it only a little or not at all" to be unbiased about candidates, according to the survey. But the picture was not entirely bleak.
Research by the nonpartisan Brennan Center for Justice found that leading chatbots pushed back against common election conspiracy theories, including claims that voting machines were rigged, even when repeatedly challenged.
"Though the chatbots often made mistakes, they also behaved as sympathetic listeners to sceptical users — while still refusing to endorse conspiracy theories," said the centre.
"This suggests they could play a constructive role in fighting election disinformation."
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 10,000 patients facing organ failure in Malaysia, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 10,036 patients in the country were facing organ failure as of Oct 15, underscoring the need for comprehensive reforms to the organ donation and transplant ecosystem, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the need was increasingly urgent given the low rate of organ donation, at just 1.33 donors per million population.
He said the establishment of the National Transplant Council (NTC) was a strategic move to strengthen governance and drive the national organ donation agenda through a whole-of-government approach, addressing weaknesses caused by agencies working in silos.
"Through the NTC, we are creating unprecedented cross-ministerial synergy. We are mobilising emergency air logistics through Mercy Flight, involving the Fire and Rescue Department and the Defence Ministry, supported by rapid police outrider escorts to prevent delays.
"We are also examining a proposal to integrate organ donor registration status into driving licences with the Transport Ministry, supported by a sustainable funding framework from the Finance Ministry and clear religious guidance from the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim)," he said in a Facebook post.
Dzulkefly said he chaired the council's first meeting this afternoon.
He said the reforms would bring three key benefits to the public, including ensuring that organ allocation was carried out more transparently and equitably based on clinical priorities.
The public would also be able to pledge their organs with greater confidence, as every process would be subject to the Human Tissues Act and strict religious fatwa requirements.
"Third, this integrated logistics chain will ensure organs reach operating theatres as quickly as possible," he said.
Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry would continue strengthening awareness campaigns through the "Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku" initiative to ensure donors' wishes were respected, including by their family members.
He said respecting donors' pledges and addressing the hopes of patients awaiting organ transplants were shared responsibilities that society must uphold.

Title: Melaka cops receive six election-related complaints
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka police have received six election-related reports since yesterday, including four involving damage to or the loss of political parties' campaign materials.
Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said the complaints involved campaign flags being broken, removed, torn, burnt and damaged in several state constituencies.
He said the reports received yesterday included the loss of or damage to 22 campaign flags in Ayer Keroh, while about 150 Pakatan Harapan (PH) flags in Rumbia were believed to have been broken.
Police also received reports of PH flags allegedly being removed in Ayer Limau and Parti Bersama campaign materials being damaged in Paya Rumput, he said in a statement.
Dzulkhairi said police had also received a report concerning remarks by Seremban MP Anthony Loke Siew Fook on the disclosure of the pardon minutes involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Another report was lodged in Jasin over the alleged distribution of food baskets and cash estimated at RM50 in conjunction with Deepavali.
The incident was also linked to the presence of a Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate's representative. The case is being investigated under Section 10 of the Election Offences Act 1954, he said.
Dzulkhairi said the Criminal Investigation Department was investigating the reports to identify those involved.
Earlier, Parti Bersama candidate for Paya Rumput Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar alleged that his party's campaign materials had been damaged, including being set on fire.
He said party election workers discovered the damage between 4am and 7am yesterday. An inspection near the Jalan Bukit Rambai bridge found several flagpoles broken and one flag burnt.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Residents recount desperate escapes as flash floods hit Kampung Melayu Subang
Article:
SUBANG: A man had to carry his elderly parents to safety after flash floods hit Kampung Melayu Subang oday, with floodwaters rising rapidly to waist level.
Zulkarnain Hashim, 46, said he carried his 90-year-old mother and 89-year-old father to higher ground as the water surged.
He said there was a heavy downpour from 2 pm to 4 pm, before water levels rose abruptly to waist level by 5pm.
"It was complete chaos when the water rose so quickly. I had to carry both my mother and father to get them to safety.
"This is not the first time. The flood problem has persisted since 1995, and this year alone our area has been flooded three times," he told Bernama.
Zulkarnain also claimed the neighbourhood's flood warning siren did not sound during the incident, raising questions about the effectiveness of the early warning system
Meanwhile, a 24-year-old mother faced an anxious ordeal getting her two children, including her four-month-old baby, out of their home as floodwaters began rising.
Nur Atilia Elina Rosli said her husband, Ahmad Nawi Yaman, 27, was at work when the water started rising around 3.20pm, just as their baby woke from a nap.
She acted swiftly to move the baby and their three-year-old child out of the house.
"It was chaotic because I have a baby. When we left, the water was already knee-deep. I had to wade through the water carrying my children to reach a house on higher ground.
"This is the worst flood we have experienced so far. The water reached chest level," she said when met at the temporary relief centre at Dewan Siantan, Kampung Melayu Subang.
Earlier, three victims, including a disabled elderly man and an infant, were evacuated to the relief centre following the afternoon deluge.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.18pm, and a fire engine from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene at 5.33 pm.
He said the flash flood affected about 92 houses across four roads, namely Lorong Merbau (30 houses), Jalan Cengal (seven), Jalan Resak (five), and Jalan Jati (50).

Title: Sri Lanka's war widows still search for the missing
Article:
SEATED outside a church, Saradhadevi Thadcanamoorty recites four handwritten pages of names — 124 husbands, fathers and brothers who vanished during Sri Lanka's civil war.
The Tamil woman, in her 60s, then picked up a placard and with three others started a "march for justice" in the busy eastern city of Batticaloa — their 1,604th consecutive day of protest.
From 1983 to 2009, Sri Lanka was ravaged by war between government forces representing the Sinhalese majority and Tamil separatist rebels, members of a largely Hindu minority.
Over 100,000 people were killed, including many civilians, according to United Nations estimates.
Tens of thousands also disappeared, or were abducted, tortured or killed by security forces or the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
More than 15 years after the war ended, the fate of most remains unknown.
Complaints, court appeals, protests, international pressure and repeated government promises have brought little progress.
Thadcanamoorty's story reflects the horrors of the war and the families' long search for answers.
In July 1992, her husband Nallathambi, 34, was found dead in his field, shot in the head.
Witnesses said a soldier had killed him. His wife immediately reported the soldier to the police.
"They told me, 'If you say your husband was killed by a soldier, they will never give him back to you'," she said.
"So I ended up filing a complaint against an unknown person. I recovered his body, received compensation of 50,000 rupees (US$151 at current rates), and the investigation stopped."
In January 2000, her son Navaneethan, 19, disappeared. She believes Tamil rebels abducted him to force him into their ranks.
"I never saw him again," she said. "In 2016, I filed a request for information with the authorities. They replied that his fate was unknown. All I was given was a certificate of disappearance — not the truth."
Lakshmi Silva has found little more certainty.
In July 1990, her husband disappeared while travelling by bus to Colombo. Armed men took him away at a checkpoint.
"Witnesses told me they were 'Tigers'," she said, referring to the rebels.
Her appeals to police and the separatists went unanswered. Those she approached warned her not to make trouble.
In 1994, a magistrate issued a death certificate. The cause of death was listed as "unknown". Since then, nothing.
"I no longer think he will come back," Lakshmi Silva admitted. Now in her 60s, she has tried to move on. "I live only for my children now," she said.
Others refuse to accept the silence.
"I have always kept hoping," said Rajeshwari Chithiravadivel, 61.
On her wall hangs a charcoal portrait of a smiling, moustachioed man, pictured between his wife and daughter.
Her husband disappeared in February 1989, abducted by masked men while shopping. The authorities issued her a death certificate in 1998.
Two years later, the Red Cross presented her with the body of a man for identification, saying it might be her husband.
"He was unrecognisable," she said. "So I continue to believe."
It is for cases like this that the women continue their daily protest, echoing Argentina's Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, who marched for years demanding answers about the children who disappeared under the country's 1976-1983 dictatorship.
"We secretly hoped thousands of people would join us, but clearly that is not the case," said Sarala Emmanuel, one of the most regular marchers and a campaigner.
"But nothing has changed — there is still a great silence," she said.
Since 2009, Sri Lankan civil society, international rights groups and the United Nations have repeatedly urged successive governments to investigate wartime crimes and bring those responsible to justice.
The election of Anura Kumara Dissanayake as president in 2024 rekindled hopes.
In his election manifesto, the country's first left-wing president promised to probe "political assassinations, disappearances and assaults" and open an independent national prosecutor's office.
Two years on, some progress had been made, said Human Rights Watch in September, but the government had failed to address "the urgent need to end impunity".
"Successive governments are worried to take any steps," said Rasamanikham R. Shanakiyan, a Tamil opposition lawmaker, noting most are Sinhala Buddhists, and that top security officials were reluctant.
"They know that it'll come back to them."
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Five China nationals arrested over scam using women's profiles to target Germans
Article:
IPOH: Police arrested five China nationals operating an investment scam syndicate targeting victims in Germany from a house in Anjung Bercham Utama.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, all men aged between 26 and 43, were detained following information received by police.
"Based on initial investigations and conversation scripts found on seized computers, police believe the syndicate ran a call centre operation to carry out non-existent online investment scams.
"The syndicate is believed to have been operating from the premises since September, targeting victims in Germany," he said in a statement.
He said the syndicate used WhatsApp and local internet access to carry out fraudulent activities, using profile pictures of attractive women to contact victims at random.
Victims were then persuaded to join investment schemes purportedly based in Germany and promised high returns in exchange for repeated payments.
He added that police seized five computers, 10 mobile phones, and four routers, estimated to be worth about RM25,000.
He said all the suspects have been remanded for four days, starting last Saturday until tomorrow, to facilitate investigations under Section 420 and Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Bersama candidate claims party flags vandalised, one set ablaze
Article:
MELAKA: A Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate in Paya Rumput has claimed that his party's flags were vandalised, with one set on fire.
Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar said party campaign workers discovered the damage between 4am and 7am yesterday.
He said an inspection near the Jalan Bukit Rambai bridge found several flagpoles broken and one flag burnt.
"Following the incident, Bersama urges the police to conduct a thorough investigation, including reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from the surrounding area.
"Firm action must be taken against any party or individual responsible for this act of vandalism to prevent a recurrence," he said after lodging a police report at the Batu Berendam police station today.
He urged all parties contesting the Melaka state election to campaign responsibly, respect the law and uphold public safety and order.
"Sabotage and excessive provocation should have no place in a democratic process.
"Instead, campaigns should be conducted peacefully and with integrity," he said.
Meanwhile, Melaka police, when contacted, said they would issue a statement on the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke credits federal-state cooperation for Sarawak transport projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strong cooperation and a close working relationship between the federal government and the Sarawak government have delivered high-impact transport development projects in the state within a short period, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said close cooperation with his deputy, Datuk Hasbi Habibollah, despite their different political backgrounds, had helped fulfil several key commitments to the people of Sarawak.
These include support for the establishment of Sarawak's own airline, the handover of Bintulu Port Authority to the state government, the introduction of the BAS.MY (http://bas.my/) public transport system in Kuching, the upgrading of Miri Airport and the construction of a new Road Transport Department (RTD) complex in Limbang.
In a video recording of his speech at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Limbang RTD branch office on Oct 28, uploaded to his Facebook page today, Loke said Sarawak's airline had been established in less than three years through strategic cooperation between both sides.
He said AirBorneo had commenced operations and taken over MASwings services, with all ATR aircraft now under AirBorneo. There are also plans for the airline to operate jet aircraft connecting Sarawak to various regional destinations.
Loke said the federal government had also fulfilled demands under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) by returning port authority powers to the state.
On land transport, he said the ministry had provided direct funding for public transport in Sarawak, which had not previously received such funding.
The BAS.MY (http://bas.my/) service was introduced in Kuching, with hopes of expanding it to other areas in the future, he said.
Loke said the new RTD complex in Limbang was the only new building construction approved for the current term, adding that the ministry would assess needs in other locations later.
On connectivity in northern Sarawak, he said the ministry of finance had approved the expansion and upgrading of Miri Airport to cope with passenger overflow and spur economic growth in surrounding areas, including Limbang Division.
He said the project would serve as an important gateway to Limbang, allowing for increased airport capacity and more flights and visitors, which would help stimulate development across the division. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah's RM1.7bil rural road projects postponed, not cancelled, says Mustapha
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rural road development projects worth RM1.7 billion in Sabah have not been cancelled but postponed pending a review and realignment of allocation ceilings, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
He said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan had provided a detailed explanation during the winding-up of the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 last Thursday.
"I stand by my statement that these projects have not been cancelled; they have only been postponed, and this has been explained in detail by the Finance Minister II.
"When the matter was raised in this House, people outside started asking questions, and the media asked as well. So, I had to respond based on the available facts. Alhamdulillah, the Finance Minister II has provided a clear explanation for our mutual understanding," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat.
The status of the projects had previously sparked controversy and questions following allegations of conflicting statements regarding the postponement of 13 rural road infrastructure projects, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
Earlier, Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau (Upko-Tuaran), when interjecting, sought clarification on the actual status of the 13 projects following a statement allegedly made by the deputy prime minister that the projects had been cancelled.
He also questioned the role of the Sabah and Sarawak Affairs portfolio in championing the issue, given that the explanation had come from the Finance Ministry.
Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), who also interjected, claimed that contractors in his constituency had informed him of receiving letters cancelling rural road development projects, and called for the matter to be addressed transparently and consistently.
In response, Mustapha said policy and project implementation matters should be discussed internally at cabinet level and should not be raised in the house, to avoid confusion among the public.
In another development, Mustapha proposed that admissions to medical programmes at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) give priority to students born in Sabah as a long-term measure to address the shortage of medical personnel in the state.
He said the proposal took into account the issue of 245 medical officers who had received placement letters but failed to report for duty in the state.
Wilfred had earlier expressed concern that the doctors' failure to report for duty had contributed to a shortage of medical personnel in many hospitals in Sabah, despite the various placement allowances provided by the government.
"We must ensure that students admitted to UMS medical programmes are Sabahans. If Sabah-born students are qualified, especially those with good academic results, this will help ensure that they remain in the state and serve in Sabah," he said.
He also proposed that a service requirement in Sabah be imposed on medical students from other states if they were admitted to the programmes.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved the RM8,798,331,500 allocation for the Prime Minister's Department's operating and development expenditure under the 2027 Budget, with a majority vote, following debate by 42 MPs.
The sitting resumes tomorrow.

Title: Selangor police dispose of RM1.71bil worth of illicit drugs
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) disposed of 37.3 tonnes of illicit drugs of various types valued at RM1.71 billion today.
Federal NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the exhibits were linked to 6,526 investigation papers involving cases from 2009 to 2025, all of which were fully resolved.
He said the drugs being disposed of included 33.5 tonnes of syabu (methamphetamine), 714 kg of ketamine, 104 kg of cannabis, 14 kg of ecstasy pills, nine kg of heroin, five kg of Erimin 5, one kg of Yaba pills, and 458 litres of MDMA.
"The disposal process will be carried out at a clinical waste treatment plant in Kuala Langat, where all exhibits will be completely destroyed in a controlled manner through high-tech and safe incineration," he said during a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters.
Also in attendance was Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar.
Meanwhile, Hussein said 45.7 tonnes of solid drugs and 60,880 litres of liquid drugs worth approximately RM1.93 billion were disposed nationwide.
"Of that total, Selangor recorded the highest disposal value at RM1.71 billion, followed by Sabah with RM120.4 million and Johor with RM40.02 million," he said.
Hussein said the NCID also disposed of 13,342 narcotics investigation papers nationwide involving cases from 1991 to 2025.
"Of that figure, 90 per cent were cases were prosecuted and sentenced in court, eight per cent were acquitted, and two per cent involved seizures without arrest.
"Selangor recorded the highest number of disposed investigation papers at 6,526 cases, followed by Sarawak with 2,383 cases, and Perak with 2,069 cases," he said.
On enforcement, Hussein said from January to October this year, the NCID recorded 184,732 cases involving 205,536 arrests nationwide in its crackdown on drug trafficking and abuse.
"During the same period, the NCID seized over 39.1 tonnes of solid drugs and 31,176.56 litres of liquid drugs, while substances seized under the Poisons Act 1952 amounted to 47 tonnes and 112,600.94 litres.
"The total value of the seized drugs and poisons is RM2.96 billion," he said.

Title: MoE steps up flood preparations for SPM candidates
Article:
KUALA NERUS: The Education Ministry is stepping up preparations for the northeast monsoon to ensure Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas can sit their examinations safely.
Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation, named Ops Payung, was aimed at ensuring candidates in flood-affected areas could take their examinations without disruption.
He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations.
"For example, SPM candidates living on islands in Terengganu will be brought to the mainland and accommodated in boarding schools. This will prevent them from having to cross rough seas during the monsoon season to reach their examination centres.
"It will also provide a safer and more suitable working environment for teachers serving as examination personnel," he told reporters after the Terafecta Digital Luminaries Awards ceremony organised by the Terengganu Education Department at Dewan Jubli Perak, Bandar Baru Kuala Nerus.
Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.
On schools designated as temporary relief centres, he said Nadma allocated more than RM7 million this year to help the ministry improve their facilities.
The allocation covered toilet repairs and school maintenance to ensure the facilities were in good condition to accommodate flood victims.
"Recently, we were also informed that Nadma would provide an additional RM5 million to support the ministry's post-northeast monsoon efforts," he said.
He advised schools, parents and students to remain vigilant and take the necessary safety precautions throughout the monsoon season.
Parents, particularly those living in flood-prone areas, were urged to keep a close watch on their children to prevent accidents.
"Children playing in floodwaters or near drains during floods can put themselves in danger. Parents should therefore pay closer attention to their children's safety. Health and hygiene must also be prioritised," he said.
Zainal said the ministry was also ready to deploy its Smart Support Team (SST), comprising counselling teachers, to provide mental health support programmes and activities for primary school pupils.
The Academic Support Team (AST) would also assist students affected by floods, including by providing academic support at temporary relief centres.
"Although the school holidays begin on Dec 5, these teams can still be deployed to flood relief centres if schools are affected by floods in November, particularly to support examination candidates," he said.
He expressed hope that preparations and coordination with Nadma, state disaster management committees, the police, the Civil Defence Force and other agencies would proceed smoothly to address any eventuality during the monsoon season.
The 2026 SPM written examinations will be held from Nov 23 to Dec 17, while the northeast monsoon began on Oct 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027.

Title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in a clash involving a group of people outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations indicated that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to determine the actual cause.
"We urge the public not to speculate about the incident as investigations are still ongoing," he told a press conference at the Cheras district police headquarters.
He said police had arrested nine people, including a woman, aged between 16 and 44, to assist in investigations and seized several items believed to have been used in the incident.
Two of those arrested, aged 32 and 44, were identified as the main suspects.
"All nine were remanded for one to three days, while six of them had previous criminal and drug-related records," he said.
Police are also tracking down about 15 others believed to have been involved in the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting with weapons.
Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station's Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department.
The arrests were made near the scene after police received information about a fight involving a group of people around 11 pm.

Title: US Senate confirms Joshua Harris as ambassador to Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United States (US) Senate has confirmed the nomination of Joshua Harris as the country's next ambassador to Malaysia.
Harris has been confirmed by the US Senate as the country's next ambassador to Malaysia, following a voice vote on Sept 30, 2026.
According to the US Congress website, Harris, from Maryland, is a career member of the US Senior Foreign Service with the rank of Minister-Counsellor.
His nomination was received from President Donald Trump on July 21, 2026, and referred to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
The committee held a hearing on Sept 16 before the nomination was discharged from further consideration by unanimous consent on Sept 30. The Senate considered and confirmed his nomination on the same day.
Harris served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of State in the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs from July 18, 2022, to Aug 5, 2025, overseeing US relations with Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia.
The ambassadorial post in Kuala Lumpur has been vacant since February following the departure of Edgard D. Kagan, who concluded his tenure as the 22nd US Ambassador to Malaysia.
Kagan, a career diplomat, presented his credentials to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, in March 2024 after being confirmed by the Senate in November 2023. -- BERNAMA

Title: KTMB confirms cargo train locomotive catches fire in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed that a cargo train locomotive caught fire at Kilometre 4.75 along the Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route around 1.10 pm today.
In a statement, KTMB said locomotive M1004 was hauling cargo train No. 193 from Port of Tanjung Pelepas to Pasir Gudang when the incident occurred.
The train driver immediately stopped the train after noticing the fire as a safety precaution.
"The fire was completely extinguished by the Fire and Rescue Department at 2.50 pm. No injuries were reported," the statement said.
KTMB said safety measures were also put in place at the affected area before trains were allowed to resume.
The locomotive was taken to the Kempas Baru Depot for technical inspection and damage assessment.
Further inspections will be conducted with Berapit Mobility and the Railway Assets Corporation (RAC) to determine the cause of the fire.
The locomotive is part of KTMB's Rolling Stock Strategy (RSS), which involves 44 locomotives and 246 cargo wagons under a sale-and-leaseback arrangement to strengthen the country's freight rail operations.
"Findings from the investigation will be reviewed to determine the necessary preventive and improvement measures. The public is advised against speculation, and further updates will be provided as they become available," the statement said.
Meanwhile, the Johor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said seven personnel from the Tebrau Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call, adding that the fire caused about five per cent damage to the locomotive.

Title: Flash floods close both directions of NKVE between Shah Alam, Setia Alam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Both directions of the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) between Shah Alam and Setia Alam have been temporarily closed after flash floods rendered a stretch of the highway impassable this evening.
Plus Malaysia Bhd said the closure involved both carriageways between Kilometre 9.1 and KM9.4, following heavy rain around 6.20pm.
As an immediate safety measure, southbound traffic from Subang was being diverted off the NKVE via the North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite).
"Meanwhile, northbound vehicles from Bukit Raja are being diverted off the NKVE at the Setia Alam Interchange," it said in a statement.
Highway users are advised to refer to Plus' official communication channels — X account @PLUSTrafik, the PLUS app, Variable Message Signs (VMS), Plus' virtual assistant PUTRI, and its official social media platforms - for the latest updates on weather and flood conditions, as well as alternative routes.
Motorists are also advised not to drive through floodwaters, as even water that appears shallow can cause vehicle engines to stall or vehicles to be swept away by strong currents.
"Please comply with all temporary signage and instructions given by our personnel at the location," Plus said.
For immediate assistance, highway users can contact PlusLine at 1-800-88-0000, use the SOS button on the Plus app or interact with Plus' virtual assistant, PUTRI.

Title: Govt finalising Child Act amendments to set clearer detention periods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is finalising the draft Children (Amendment) Bill 2026 for submission to the cabinet for consideration, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M Kulasegaran.
He said the proposed amendments aimed to improve Section 97 of the Child Act following the abolition of mandatory death sentences and life imprisonment in 2023.
He said the changes would introduce a more proportionate sentencing framework and prevent juvenile offenders from being imprisoned indefinitely without a specified detention period.
Under the existing Section 97(2) of the Act, courts must order child offenders to be detained in prison at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong or the Ruler of the relevant state, without specifying a maximum detention period.
"The Madani Government is committed to improving this legal framework to ensure a clearer and more proportionate sentencing approach that takes into account the principles of justice for children as well as public safety," he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said a Special Committee to Review and Amend Section 97 of the Act had been established to examine proposed improvements to the provision, taking into account the principles of the best interests of the child, rehabilitation and reintegration, as well as international best practices.
Kulasegaran said the findings of the review had led to the cabinet's agreement on Sept 30 to four policy decisions concerning the proposed amendments.
He said the proposed policy decisions were then presented to the Conference of Rulers on Oct 14 for consideration and deliberation.
Meanwhile, on the proposal to establish a Law Drafting Unit in Parliament, Kulasegaran said the move was progressive and in line with efforts to strengthen the independence and autonomy of the country's legislative institution.
"This matter merits consideration within the framework of implementing the Parliamentary Services Act 2025, subject to deliberation by the Parliamentary Service Council and the relevant staffing and legal requirements," he said.
He said the establishment of the unit would enable parliament to develop its own legislative drafting expertise, particularly to assist members of parliament in preparing Private Members' Bills and proposed amendments to legislation without having to rely entirely on the drafting expertise of the executive.

Title: Puchong slaughterhouse not under Jakim's halal monitoring, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A chicken slaughterhouse suspected of operating without local authority permits was not listed in the Department of Islamic Development (Jakim)'s monitoring records because it did not have halal certification.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said preliminary inspections found that the premises in Puchong was also processing and distributing fresh chicken without the necessary approvals.
"Jakim views this issue seriously as it involves Syariah compliance, hygiene, and public confidence in the halal status of chicken in the market.
"All operational and sales records of this premises are not in the halal certification monitoring records of Jakim or the respective State Islamic Religious Departments," he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said halal certification authority in Malaysia is governed under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 through the Trade Descriptions (Certification and Marking of Halal) Order 2011.
In addition, a slaughterhouse scheme was introduced to enable operators to apply for the halal certification ensuring slaughtering and animal handling comply with Syariah principles and halal certification requirements.
Zulkifli said Jakim, together with State Islamic Religious Departments and State Islamic Religious Councils, enforces oversight through halal certification, audits, and monitoring of premises that hold the halal certification.
He said audits cover animal sources, qualifications of slaughterers and halal supervisors, stunning methods, slaughtering processes, hygiene, product handling, and halal management systems.
However, as halal certification in Malaysia is voluntary, he noted that regulating all slaughterhouses requires cross-agency cooperation with local authorities, the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS), the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, and other enforcement agencies according to their respective jurisdictions.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said Jakim continues to intensify joint inspections, intelligence sharing, and investigations into complaints to protect consumer interests and preserve the integrity of the halal poultry supply chain.
For products or premises suspected of using misleading halal logos or statements, Jakim collaborates with the domestic trade and cost of living ministry and relevant agencies to conduct verification and investigations.
"Stationing halal supervisors at abattoirs is a mandatory condition for any slaughterhouse applying for the Malaysian Halal Certification," he said.
Zulkifli said Jakim had taken action in several past cases, including issuing compounds totalling RM40,000 against three companies for regulatory non-compliance.
On Oct 30, more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken, which was processed without complying with Syariah slaughtering regulations and halal requirements, were seized during a raid on a warehouse in Puchong, Selangor.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing chicken at the premises, were also detained during the operation, codenamed Ops Taring Chiller.

Title: Strong winds rip roofs off houses in Kulim [WATCH]
Article:

Madie, who lives in Taman Selasih, said he was outside running errands when the incident happened and saw several house roofs being blown away by the wind.

Title: Cop held over RM15,000 in bribes to protect drug trafficking activities
Article:
ALOR STAR: A policeman has been arrested for allegedly soliciting and accepting about RM15,000 in bribes from a drug dealer in exchange for protecting drug trafficking activities in the state from enforcement action.
The man, in his 30s, was detained about 2pm today when he arrived to record his statement at the Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office.
Investigations indicated the offences took place throughout 2024.
He is believed to have received monthly payments of between RM200 and RM2,500 through transfers into his personal bank account.
Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong confirmed the arrest.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries up to 20 years' jail and a minimum fine of five times the bribe amount or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

Title: Four vehicles, car workshop destroyed in Rembau fire
Article:
REMBAU: Four vehicles and a car workshop were destroyed in a fire at Batu 17, Chembong.
A Negri Sembilan Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said it received a call about the fire at a workshop opposite Masjid Kariah Chembong at 6.50pm.
A team from the Rembau Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched. They were assisted by personnel from the Kota Fire and Rescue Station.
The spokesman said information from Operations Commander Mohd Kassim Arippin confirmed the workshop was completely destroyed in the blaze.
Four vehicles inside the workshop were also destroyed.

Title: Mubarak mobilises veterans to support BN in Melaka election
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional's campaign in the Melaka election is receiving support from the Malaysian Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak), which is mobilising its members, veterans and retirees to reach out to voters ahead of polling on Nov 14.
State BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said Mubarak was actively engaging voters through its network to garner support for the coalition.
"They are enthusiastic about building a blue wave and keeping that momentum going until polling day.
"I am grateful to Mubarak because, although they retired long ago, their fighting spirit remains strong," he said after attending the Melaka Mubarak Loyal Partners programme.
Present were Mubarak president Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman and its Melaka chairman, Datuk Nazari Adzim.
Rauf, who is caretaker chief minister, said some members, despite being 80 years old, remained active in the campaign to pass on their experience and commitment to the next generation.
"These efforts are important for the next generation to understand the meaning of struggle and sacrifice, and to carry on what has been handed down to them," he said.
Aziz said Mubarak aimed to secure votes for BN from an estimated 100,000 people, including its members, relatives and friends.
He said the estimate took into account the wider reach of more than 20,000 members of its loyal partners network, which comprises 24 non-governmental organisations and associations, as well as six veterans' groups.
Aziz said he was confident in the strategy, citing its use in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, where it helped BN win seats.
"Mubarak supreme council members from Pahang, Johor, Selangor, Kelantan, Kedah, Kuala Lumpur and Perlis are already on the ground helping with the campaign to ensure BN retains Melaka.
"We hope the blue wave that began in Johor and passed through Negri Sembilan will reach Melaka on the night of Nov 14," he added.

Title: Aceh worker escapes death penalty, jailed 7 years for drug possession
Article:
MELAKA: A worker from Aceh escaped the death penalty after being sentenced to seven years in prison and 10 strokes of the cane for possessing 58.23g of methamphetamine.
Musliadi A Rahman, 40, committed the offence in 2024 and was sentenced by the High Court after pleading guilty to an alternative charge.
High Court judge Datuk DJP Suria Kumar said he had considered the facts of the case, the defence's plea for leniency and the prosecution's submissions. He ordered the prison term to run from the date of Musliadi's arrest on Aug 15, 2024.
"Remember, Musliadi, do not get involved in drug activities again. You should be grateful that your lawyer's representation was accepted and the charge reduced. This is an opportunity for you," he said.
Under the alternative charge, Musliadi was accused of possessing the drugs at a house in Jalan Sg 10, Taman Seri Gamelan, Kuala Sungai Baru, Alor Gajah, at about 11pm on Aug 15, 2024.
He was charged under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39A(2) of the same Act. The provision carries a sentence of life imprisonment or a minimum of five years' imprisonment, and at least 10 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
According to the case facts, a team of Customs officers raided a house in Taman Seri Gamelan, Kuala Sungai Baru, where they found two Indonesian men, including Musliadi.
A search of the sofa where Musliadi had been sitting led officers to a shoulder bag he had concealed. Inside, they found several packets containing crystalline substances suspected to be methamphetamine.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Anida Mohd Nasir appeared for the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, while Musliadi was represented by lawyer Ho Zhi Qian.
The prosecution had sought a prison term of between 12 and 13 years, along with 10 strokes of the cane, citing the public interest, the seriousness of the offence and the amount of methamphetamine seized, which exceeded the 30g threshold under Section 39A(2) of the Act.
The defence sought a lighter sentence, saying Musliadi had no previous convictions and had shown remorse by pleading guilty as soon as the alternative charge was offered, saving the court time and costs.
Musliadi came to Malaysia in 2009 and worked as a labourer in Kuantan, Klang and Melaka to support his wife, two children and elderly mother in his home country.

Title: Rembayung introduces new booking system to curb scalpers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Popular restaurant Rembayung has introduced a new reservation system in collaboration with Grab to curb scalping and prevent the resale of bookings.
Content creator and entrepreneur Khairul Aming, whose real name is Khairul Amin Kamarulzaman, announced the changes in a Threads post, saying each verified Grab user would be limited to one reservation every two weeks.
Under the new system, reservations are non-transferable. Customers must bring the phone used to make the booking and open the Grab application before entering the restaurant.
Screenshots of reservations will not be accepted, he said.
Bookings through Grab are available from today.
Khairul Aming expressed hope that the new measures would help reduce scalping, which has been a concern among customers trying to secure reservations at the restaurant.
